(a) Report.—Not later than 180 days after the date of the enactment of this Act, the Secretary of Defense, in coordination with the Director of National Intelligence, shall submit to the appropriate congressional committees a report on the advisability and feasibility of using available spacecraft assets of the space-based infrared system wide-field-of-view program to satisfy other mission requirements of the Department of Defense or the intelligence community. 
    (b) Matters Covered.—The report required by subsection (a) shall include, at a minimum, the following:
        (1) An evaluation of using the space-based infrared system wide-field-of-view spacecraft bus for other urgent national security space priorities. 
        (2) An evaluation of the cost and schedule impact, if any, to the space-based infrared system wide-field-of-view program if the spacecraft bus is used for another purpose.  
    (c) Form.—The report required by subsection (a) shall be submitted in unclassified form, but may contain a classified annex if necessary to protect the national security interests of the United States. 
    (d) Appropriate Congressional Committees Defined.—In this section, the term “appropriate congressional committees” means—
        (1) the congressional defense committees; and 
        (2) the Permanent Select Committee on Intelligence of the House of Representatives and the Select Committee on Intelligence of the Senate.

fable.w: The tempting reading is that "in coordination with" and a required report signal participation. But the coordination is between two federal officials (the Secretary of Defense and the Director of National Intelligence), and the report goes to congressional committees, so every actor is inside the federal government. No outside party such as states, experts, industry, or the public is consulted, and there is no rulemaking, hearing, or right to sue.
fable.s: the Secretary of Defense, in coordination with the Director of National Intelligence, shall submit to the appropriate congressional committees a report

qwen_block.w: The section requires the Secretary of Defense to submit a report to congressional committees. The coordination mentioned is between two federal officials (Secretary of Defense and Director of National Intelligence), which is intra-governmental. The recipient of the report is Congress, which is inside the federal government. Therefore, no outside parties are involved in the decision-making process.
qwen_block.s: the Secretary of Defense, in coordination with the Director of National Intelligence, shall submit to the appropriate congressional committees a report

opus.w: The only coordination here is between the Secretary of Defense and the Director of National Intelligence, and both are federal officials. The report goes to congressional committees, which are also part of the federal government. The words "coordination" and "report" might suggest participation, but no state, tribe, company, expert or member of the public takes part in any federal decision.
opus.s: the Secretary of Defense, in coordination with the Director of National Intelligence, shall submit to the appropriate congressional committees a report

qwen_chat.w: The section requires a report to be submitted to Congress by the Secretary of Defense, in coordination with the Director of National Intelligence. Both the Secretary of Defense and the Director of National Intelligence are federal officials, and Congress is part of the federal government. Therefore, all actors involved are inside the federal government, and no outside parties are consulted or involved in the decision-making process.
qwen_chat.s: the Secretary of Defense, in coordination with the Director of National Intelligence, shall submit to the appropriate congressional committees a report
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that "coordination" with the Director of National Intelligence implies participation. However, both the Secretary of Defense and the Director of National Intelligence are federal officials inside the government. Intra-governmental coordination does not constitute participation under the definition. Furthermore, the report is submitted to Congress, which is also inside the federal government. There is no involvement of outside parties (states, tribes, public, experts, etc.) in the decision-making process described.
